messages:
Jenna Park: customer reported tool-calling failure for a compound workflow. They call two tools in parallel (websearch + fetch_invoice) via function-calling and the LLM returns a response that includes websearch output but attributes it to fetch_invoice. 

Sam Ortiz: can you paste the minimal repro and any raw API request/response we have?

Jenna Park: here's the anonymized request/response from the customer (POST to /v1/generate). Note: they use function_call: "auto" and supply two tools.

Jenna Park: ```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer sk-...
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "model": "rwd-ggml-13b",
  "input": "Find invoice 1234 and summarize the last payment.",
  "functions": [
    {
      "name": "websearch",
      "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"q": {"type": "string"}}}
    },
    {
      "name": "fetch_invoice",
      "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"id": {"type": "string"}}}
    }
  ],
  "function_call": "auto"
}
```

Jenna Park: customer logs show the tool_result array: ```[{"tool_name":"websearch","output":"Found blog post..."},{"tool_name":"fetch_invoice","output":"{\"id\":\"1234\",\"last_payment\":\"$200\"}"}]``` but final LLM message was: "fetch_invoice returned: Found blog post..." which is wrong.

Sam Ortiz: ugh. do we have any correlation ids in the raw runtime logs? need to see tool_result.id or call_id mapping.

Marco Liu: eng-runtime: when we dispatch parallel tool calls we tag each subcall with an internal call_id; the model's reasoning must map tool_outputs back by call_id. If outputs are returned out-of-order and we rely on array index instead of explicit id mapping that could cause cross-association.

Priya Desai: customer claims intermittent: small fraction of requests only and seems to spike under moderate concurrency (~30rps).

Jenna Park: steps to repro we used in support env: 1) run parallel tool-calls with two fast and one slow tool to force out-of-order return 2) use function_call auto 3) run 200 concurrent requests 4) check final model message attribution. I attached a runnable curl below.

Jenna Park: ```
# minimal repro (customer)
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REPRO_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-ggml-13b","input":"Get doc","functions":[{"name":"fast_tool","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{} }},{"name":"slow_tool","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{}}}],"function_call":"auto"}' &
done
wait
```

Sam Ortiz: thanks. can you pull the runtime log for one failing request (trace id 0x9f3a2b from customer)?

Jenna Park: pasted below from request 0x9f3a2b (scrubbed):

Jenna Park: ```
[2025-10-02T14:03:12Z] route incoming req id=0x9f3a2b model=rwd-ggml-13b
[2025-10-02T14:03:12Z] dispatch tool call id=call_7a name=fast_tool
[2025-10-02T14:03:12Z] dispatch tool call id=call_7b name=slow_tool
[2025-10-02T14:03:12Z] tool call completed id=call_7a -> output id=out_fa (fast)
[2025-10-02T14:03:13Z] tool call completed id=call_7b -> output id=out_sb (slow)
[2025-10-02T14:03:13Z] assembled tool_results: [out_sb, out_fa]  # <- looks flipped
[2025-10-02T14:03:13Z] final model input constructed with tool_results mapping by index
[2025-10-02T14:03:13Z] model generated message: fetch_invoice returned: Found blog post...
```

Priya Desai: that assembled tool_results line is telling — looks like a race where we append as they arrive but then map back to function list by index. Should map via call_id -> function_name.

EngOncall: acknowledging, assigning to eng-runtime. tagging @Marco.

Marco Liu: I'll take it. initial hypothesis: our optimization to reduce memory copies concatenates tool outputs into a shared buffer and we had a bug that used buffer ordering rather than explicit call_id mapping during the final construction phase. Repro locally with our harness.

Marco Liu: quick mitigation: force serial tool completion aggregation (cheap toggle) in runtime so we don't reorder. I'll push a flag to canary.

Sam Ortiz: can we provide customer workaround meanwhile? Jenna, please ask them to either 1) set function_call to explicit name sequence (call sequentially) or 2) include a unique id in each tool args (e.g., {call_id: "c1"}) and make sure the tool echoes it back so the LLM can disambiguate.

Jenna Park: told customer the workaround and asked for permission to run a canary toggle. They agreed.

Marco Liu: PR opened #rwd-runtime/452. Quickfix: change final assembly to map outputs by call_id; fallback to index only if call_id missing. Adding regression test with heavy concurrency and slow/fast mix.

Marco Liu: note: also found a schema validation hole — some tools return JSON strings (escaped JSON) instead of objects and our assembler sometimes treated them as raw strings, which can further confuse mapping when we attempt to parse. I'll add stricter parsing + schema lint.

EngOncall: rolling canary toggle to 10% in prod region eu-west-1 now. monitoring trace rate and attribution errors.

Sam Ortiz: timeline?

Marco Liu: aiming for full roll within 24 hours if canary looks good. regression test + code review in next 3 hours.

Jenna Park: ticket created SUP-4921 referencing PR and customer case. Provided customer ETA. They were receptive.

Priya Desai: postmortem items: 1) add unit/regression tests for parallel tool ordering 2) ensure tool_result objects always include call_id 3) add metric for mismatched attribution count 4) docs note: recommend callers include call_id for critical workflows.

Sam Ortiz: good. also verify billing isn't double-charging when calls bounce — I saw another thread where out-of-order assembly caused duplicate retries. Jenna, confirm billing hooks for this trace were a single invoice.

Jenna Park: billing checks out for this trace. no duplicate billing.

Marco Liu: after fix deployed, will run extended load test (24h). will post results here.

Jenna Park: customer notified. closing loop when full roll completes. thanks everyone. :handshake:
